svg.title: The math, code and reason stack
svg.desc: Three horizontal layers. Reason, at the top, is the language model: Claude Sonnet turns profile text into attribute scores and Claude Haiku grades replies and narrates facts; it never decides and never computes the answer. Code, in the middle, decides what is allowed and what is exact: a regex gate before the model, override functions after it, largest-remainder rounding, checks to the dollar, and a replay harness that reproduced 5,501 of 5,501 past routing decisions. Math, at the bottom, decides what is best and how likely: integer programs in PuLP with the CBC solver, min-cost flow, NumPy Monte Carlo at 10,000 runs, POMDP and counterfactual regret minimization, giving the same answer for the same input at any model temperature. A request enters at the top left and travels down through code into math. The decision travels back up the right side through code before the model writes the answer.
svg.text: Three layers, one request
A request arrives
The answer leaves
REASON
Reads what arrives, writes what leaves
Claude Sonnet: profile text into attribute scores
Claude Haiku: grades replies, narrates facts
Never decides, never computes the answer
CODE
Decides what is allowed and what is exact
Regex gate before the model, overrides after it
Largest-remainder rounding, checks to the dollar
Replay harness: 5,501 of 5,501 past decisions
MATH
Decides what is best and how likely
PuLP and CBC integer programs, min-cost flow
NumPy Monte Carlo at 10,000 runs, POMDP, CFR
Same input, same answer, at any temperature
Down the left, the model's reading becomes fields that code validates.
Up the right, the solver's decision is checked by code before
the model is allowed to write a word about it.
